ruleset.name: jpinpoint-remoting-rules
ruleset.description: jPinpoint rule set for performance aware Kotlin coding, sponsored by Rabobank.

rule.name: AvoidXMLGregorianCalendar
rule.message: XMLGregorianCalendar is used. It is slow in JAXB.
rule.description: Problem: XMLGregorianCalendar is a large object involving substantial processing. It is created with the poorly performing DatatypeFactory. Solution: Add a converter for alternative date handling with java.time. (jpinpoint-rules)

property.name: xpath

rule.name: AvoidObjectMapperAsField
rule.message: Avoid ObjectMapper as field, use ObjectReader or ObjectWriter instead.
rule.description: Problem: Configuring an ObjectMapper is not thread-safe. Solution: Create ObjectReaders and ObjectWriters from ObjectMapper and only share those as a property, since they are immutable and therefore thread-safe. Exception: convertValue is not provided by ObjectReader/ObjectWriter; suppress the rule in that case. (jpinpoint-rules)

property.name: xpath

rule.name: ObjectMapperCreatedForEachMethodCall
rule.message: An ObjectMapper or JsonMapper is created for each method call, which is expensive.
rule.description: Problem: Jackson ObjectMapper/JsonMapper creation is expensive because it does much class loading. Solution: Since ObjectMapper/JsonMapper objects are thread-safe after configuration in one thread, they can be shared afterward between requests and reused. Reuse created instances from a companion object or top-level val. (jpinpoint-rules)

rule.name: GsonCreatedForEachMethodCall
rule.message: A Gson object is created for each method call, which is expensive.
rule.description: Problem: Gson creation is relatively expensive. Solution: Since Gson objects are thread-safe after creation, they can be shared between threads. Reuse created instances from a companion object or top-level val. (jpinpoint-rules)

rule.name: HttpClientBuilderWithoutDisableConnectionState
rule.message: A HttpClient builder is used and disableConnectionState is not called. HTTP client tracks connection state while using TLS.
rule.description: Problem: NTLM authenticated connections and SSL/TLS connections with client certificate authentication are stateful: they have a specific user identity/security context per session. If HttpClients have enabled connection state tracking which is the default, established TLS connections will not be reused because it is assumed that the user identity or security context may differ. Then performance will suffer due to a full TLS handshake for each request. Solution: HttpClients should disable connection state tracking in order to reuse TLS connections, since service calls for one pool have the same user identity/security context for all sessions. (jpinpoint-rules)

property.name: xpath
property.value: (:locally created http client builder without disableConnectionState :) //PostfixUnarySuffix//NavigationSuffix[@Identifier="custom" and ancestor::PostfixUnaryExpression/PrimaryExpression/@Identifier="HttpClients" and not(ancestor::PostfixUnaryExpression/PostfixUnarySuffix/NavigationSuffix/@Identifier="disableConnectionState")] , //PostfixUnarySuffix//NavigationSuffix[@Identifier="create" and ancestor::PostfixUnaryExpression/PrimaryExpression[(@Identifier="HttpClientBuilder" or @Identifier="HttpAsyncClientBuilder") and not(ancestor::PostfixUnaryExpression/PostfixUnarySuffix/NavigationSuffix/@Identifier="disableConnectionState")]] , (: method param http client builder without disableConnectionState :) //FunctionValueParameter/Parameter/Type/TypeReference/UserType/SimpleUserType[(@Identifier="HttpClients" or @Identifier="HttpClientBuilder" or @Identifier="HttpAsyncClientBuilder") and not(ancestor::FunctionDeclaration//PostfixUnarySuffix/NavigationSuffix/@Identifier="disableConnectionState")]

rule.example: private fun createHttpClientBuilder(properties: ConnectionProperties) = HttpClients.custom() .setDefaultRequestConfig(createRequestConfig(properties)) .setMaxConnTotal(properties.maxConnTotal) .setMaxConnPerRoute(properties.maxConnPerRoute) // violation, no disableConnectionState() call

rule.name: HttpClientBuilderWithoutTimeouts
rule.message: Apache HttpClient builder is used and not all three timeouts are configured.
rule.description: Problem: for connectionRequestTimeout, connectTimeout, socketTimeout (using HttpComponentsClientHttpRequestFactory/RequestConfig) or readTimeout/responseTimeout (using RequestConfig v4/v5) and connectTimeout (using ConnectionConfig v5) the default timeout settings are not optimal in most cases. Solution: Set the timeouts explicitly to proper reasoned values. See best practice values via the link. Use the setDefaultRequestConfig with a method with a RequestConfig object on HttpClient builders to set the timeouts. (jpinpoint-rules)

rule.name: AvoidDeprecatedHystrix
rule.message: Netflix Hystrix is deprecated. Use an alternative like resilience4j
rule.description: Problem: Hystrix is not actively maintained anymore. Solution: Netflix recommends to use open source alternatives like resilience4j. (jpinpoint-rules)

rule.name: HttpClientBuilderWithoutPoolSize
rule.message: HttpClient builder connection pool is not configured.
rule.description: Problem: when the [default max connections per route] external calls are being made to the same host, the next thread requesting a connection to that host must wait for a free connection. For Apache HttpClient v4, this default = 2 and for v5 this default = 5, often too low. Max total connections are 20 and 25 respectively. Solution: HttpClients should explicitly define the number of connections per route. If only one route is used, make the max number of connections equal to conn per route. Solution: 1. use setConnectionManager and call setMaxTotal and setDefaultMaxPerRoute on that connection manager, or 2. use no ConnectionManager, call setMaxConnTotal and setMaxConnPerRoute on the client directly (v4 only). (jpinpoint-rules)

property.name: xpath

rule.example:
fun bad(conMgr: Any?): HttpClient = HttpClientBuilder.create() // bad, missing setMaxConnPerRoute/setMaxConnTotal or setConnectionManager .build()
fun goodWithMgr(conMgr: Any?): HttpClient = HttpClientBuilder.create() .setConnectionManager(conMgr) // good, delegated to manager .build()
fun goodWithSizes(): HttpClient = HttpClients.custom() .setMaxConnPerRoute(MAX_CONNECTIONS) .setMaxConnTotal(MAX_CONNECTIONS) .build()

rule.name: NettyConnectionProviderWithoutMaxOrTimeout
rule.message: Netty ConnectionProvider has no defined maxConnections or pendingAcquireTimeout.
rule.description: Problem: If a Reactor Netty Connection Provider is built without an explicit `maxConnections`, this defaults to `max(#CPU, 8) * 2`. This is often too low, leading to throttling, delays and too long response times. If the provider is built without an explicit `pendingAcquireTimeout`, this defaults to `45s`. This is often too high, leading to unnecessary long waiting times. Solution: Define both `maxConnections` and `pendingAcquireTimeout` with proper values, for instance, `50` and `300 [ms]` respectively. (jpinpoint-rules)

rule.name: BufferingClientHttpRequestFactoryIsMemoryGreedy
rule.message: BufferingClientHttpRequestFactory buffers entire response bodies in memory and is memory greedy.
rule.description: Problem: BufferingClientHttpRequestFactory buffers the entire response body in memory, which is memory greedy and can cause OutOfMemoryError for large responses. Solution: Avoid using BufferingClientHttpRequestFactory. If you need to read the response body multiple times, prefer streaming approaches. (jpinpoint-rules)

rule.name: AvoidHttpHostOneArgumentConstructor
rule.message: HttpHost with only hostname uses default port, which may be confusing or incorrect.
rule.description: Problem: Creating an HttpHost with only a hostname uses a default port (-1), which can lead to confusing behaviour. Solution: Always specify the port and protocol explicitly. (jpinpoint-rules)

rule.name: AvoidJAXBUtil
rule.message: JAXB utility class recreates JAXBContext for each call, which is expensive.
rule.description: Problem: The JAXB utility class (javax.xml.bind.JAXB / jakarta.xml.bind.JAXB) recreates a JAXBContext on each call, which is CPU-intensive due to class scanning. Solution: Create and cache a JAXBContext instance and reuse it. (jpinpoint-rules)
